unmeasured: x86_64 CPU: there is no x86_64 pack binary or image (new infrastructure, not planned)
Graviton generation split: the production pack image cannot print its CPU generation, so host heterogeneity on Fargate is observable only as run-to-run spread across repeats
a fresh A10G run: the A10G noise is already recorded in each run's rescore-noise.json; no GPU job is started
the second set of a refused leg: pack_laya reports only the FIRST drifted set (exposing it is a decide-crate change, D-15)
notes: Every number in legs and controls was produced on this host by the pinned binary named in `binary`; references are copied from the files their `from` / `read_from` fields name.

pack_laya reports a RescoreDrift refusal for the FIRST drifted set only: a refused leg measures one set, and the other set is not measured on that CPU. Exposing it would need a decide-crate change, which D-15 and D-05 forbid here.
A pack leg's scratch .apr is hashed against its PACKED line and removed (807 MB each); its sha256 is the record.

The noise reference of a CUDA run is the A10G figure from its rescore-noise.json; of an MPS run, the MPS figure from its rescore-noise.json. The bound is max(floor, k x that noise), so the ratio max_abs / noise is the drift in units of the training-device noise the bound was built from.
Wall times are from a desktop machine running the legs one at a time; other load was not controlled.
No x86_64 CPU is measured: there is no x86_64 pack binary or image. The Graviton legs are generated by aws-plan and run by the owner in 14-21. No contract was amended (D-15).
